name: Cabergoline
summary: A prescription pill that lowers high prolactin by acting like dopamine on the pituitary; approved for hyperprolactinemia, including prolactin-making pituitary tumors.
what_it_is: Cabergoline is an ergot-derived dopamine agonist that binds strongly to D2 receptors and directly blocks prolactin release from the pituitary gland. Too much prolactin can cause breast milk discharge (galactorrhea) and stop periods; in trials, cabergoline restored periods and stopped discharge in most women. It stays in the body a long time, with an estimated half-life of 63 to 69 hours.

evidence.why: FDA-approved for hyperprolactinemia based on randomized trials, including one where 77% reached normal prolactin versus 59% with bromocriptine; a 2021 Cochrane review supports off-label use to prevent ovarian hyperstimulation.

status_us.label: FDA-approved for high prolactin (hyperprolactinemia)
status_us.note: Approved for hyperprolactinemic disorders in adults, either of unknown cause or due to pituitary adenomas; the label says not to use it to suppress breast milk after childbirth. Other uses, such as preventing ovarian hyperstimulation during IVF, are off-label.

benefits.claim: Brought prolactin to normal in 77% of women with hyperprolactinemia versus 59% with bromocriptine over 8 weeks, restoring periods in 77% and stopping milk discharge in 73%
In a 4-week placebo-controlled study, 74% to 95% reached normal prolactin, versus none on placebo
Dopamine agonists, including cabergoline, probably cut moderate or severe ovarian hyperstimulation in women at high risk during IVF, from about 27% to 8% to 14% (22 trials, 3,171 women; off-label)

risks.risk: Nausea (27%), headache, dizziness (15%), constipation (10%), fatigue and dizziness on standing

Heart valve damage, reported mostly at the higher amounts once used for Parkinson's disease but also in hyperprolactinemia; in people treated for hyperprolactinemia, a meta-analysis of 13 studies found more tricuspid regurgitation (odds ratio 3.74), of unclear clinical importance
Scarring (fibrosis) of the lungs and pleura, the lining around the heart, or the tissue behind the abdomen
Impulse control problems such as compulsive gambling, spending or sexual urges; psychosis and aggression have also been reported
Using dopamine agonists to stop breast milk after childbirth has been linked to high blood pressure, stroke, heart attack, seizures and death

avoid_if: History of heart valve disease or pericardial fibrosis
History of lung, pleural or retroperitoneal fibrosis
Severe liver impairment, pregnancy or the weeks after childbirth (dopamine agonists are generally avoided)
interactions: Dopamine blockers (phenothiazines, butyrophenones, thioxanthenes, metoclopramide): not recommended together
Other drugs linked to heart valve disease: only if the expected benefit outweighs the risk
Blood pressure-lowering drugs: higher risk of dizziness or fainting on standing

during: Echocardiogram every 6 to 12 months or as clinically indicated
labs.why: The label calls for an echocardiogram before starting and repeat scans every 6 to 12 months to check the heart valves, plus blood pressure checks; prolactin shows whether treatment is working.

studies.title: Dopamine agonists for preventing ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
studies.people: 3,171 women at high risk of ovarian hyperstimulation in 22 randomized trials
studies.finding: Dopamine agonists probably reduce moderate or severe ovarian hyperstimulation (odds ratio 0.32); effects on live birth and side effects are uncertain.

studies.title: A Meta-Analysis of the Prevalence of Cardiac Valvulopathy in Patients With Hyperprolactinemia Treated With Cabergoline
studies.people: Patients treated for hyperprolactinemia in 13 case-control studies
studies.finding: Tricuspid regurgitation was more common with cabergoline than in controls (odds ratio 3.74), but no patient had symptoms from it and no other valve problem was increased.

studies.title: Cabergoline tablets: Prescribing Information
studies.people: Women with hyperprolactinemia (8-week comparison with bromocriptine)
studies.finding: 77% reached normal prolactin with cabergoline versus 59% with bromocriptine, and more had periods restored and milk discharge resolved.

ask_your_clinician: Do I need an echocardiogram before starting, and how often should it be repeated?
What is causing my high prolactin, and does it need further tests?
Which mood, behavior or impulse changes should I report?

notes_for_editor: Label is the June 2026 generic cabergoline label (Greenstone, registrant Pfizer, reported to Viatris) as reprinted by Drugs.com; the Dostinex brand label was not checked. Off-label use by men on testosterone or anabolic steroids, and claims about libido, orgasm or recovery time, were not reviewed this round; no source supporting them was opened. Lowering high prolactin from any cause falls under the approved hyperprolactinemia indication. The Cochrane OHSS result pools cabergoline with bromocriptine and quinagolide. The valve meta-analysis was read as an abstract; it did not report absolute rates or a link to cumulative dose.
